title: All-optical Mechanobiology Interrogation of Yes-associated Protein in Human Cancer and Normal Cells using a Multi-functional System
protocol: Generate stable CRISPR/Cas9-edited human lung cancer cell line (PC9) and human bronchial epithelial cell line (Beas2B) that endogenously express mNeonGreen21-10/11-tagged YAP protein.
Perform PCR to amplify the DNA sequence coding for the 11th strand of the fluorescence protein, mNeonGreen2.
Knock-in the amplified DNA sequence into the YAP genomic locus of the PC9 and Beas2B cell lines using CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing system.
Check CRISPR/Cas9-engineered mNeonGreen2 expression using an epifluorescence microscope.
Use a 488 nm laser (47.5 mW/mm²) for excitation, a 40x objective (numerical aperture (NA) = 0.95), and a band-pass emission filter (ET525/50 nm) for fluorescence measurement.
Measure, quantify, and compare the fluorescence intensities using ImageJ software.
Compare the presence of fluorescence intensity in CRISPR/Cas9-engineered cells to that in parental cells (control).
Extract genomic DNA from CRISPR/Cas9-edited cell lines.
Perform PCR using primers flanking the genomic insert.
Sequence to confirm correct insertion of mNeonGreen211 at the desired loci.
Knock down mNeonGreen211 using the CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing system.
Check fluorescence intensity reduction in cells using the same microscope systems and imaging parameters as described previously.
Compare fluorescence intensities with control cell lines that have not undergone knock-down or parental cells.
Trypsinize cells to prepare them for FACS sorting.
Resuspend trypsinized cells in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Sort cells with mNeonGreen2 fluorescence above the background level of parental cell lines through two enriching rounds of FACS.
Culture PC9 and Beas2B cells in 75 cm² flasks with RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 100 μg/mL penicillin-streptomycin.
Subculture both cell lines when confluency reaches ~80%.
Test both cell lines for mycoplasma every 3 months using a detection kit, following all manufacturer's protocols strictly.
Store the cell lines in a -80°C freezer.
Use cell lines <20 passages from thaw for experiments.
Connect the confocal controller and inverted microscope to the computer.
Install software platform (Table of Materials).
Turn on the confocal controller and inverted microscope.
Launch Elements.
Open control panels of the confocal, laser, and inverted microscope in Elements.
Check movement of motorized stage.
Switch microscope objectives.
Test spatial scanning of laser lines.
Install IntelliJ, Java Development Kit 14.0, µManager version 2.0 gamma, and Fiji ImageJ on computer.
Open AMFIP project downloaded from GitHub in IntelliJ.
Click Settings | Compiler | Annotation Processors and check Enable annotation processing.
Click on Project Structure | Artifacts and create a JAR file.
Set the output directory to mmplugins under the µManager directory.
Click on Project Structure | Libraries and add mmplugins and plugins under the µManager directory.
Click on Add Configuration under the Run drop-down menu and create an application.
Enter ij.ImageJ into the Main class.
Enter -Xmx3000m -Dforce.annotation.index=true into VM option.
Set the µManager directory to the Work directory.
Click on Run to activate µManager with the AMFIP plugin.
Connect µManager with the inverted microscope.
Add the adaptive driver of the inverted microscope21 to the µManager directory.
Open µManager.
Click on Devices | Hardware Configuration Wizard and create a new configuration.
Add the Ti2 driver under Available Devices.
Select all peripheral devices and save the new configuration file.
Restart µManager and select the configuration file in step 3.2.4 in Micro-Manager Startup Configuration.
Treat the glass coverslip with 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane for 7 min at room temperature (24 °C).
Use deionized (DI) water to rinse the glass coverslip.
Dry the glass coverslip for 20 min at 160 °C.
Treat the glass coverslip with 0.5% glutaraldehyde for 30 min.
Rinse the treated coverslip with distilled water.
Mix acrylamide solution, N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide (bis) solution, and fluorescent beads suspended in 10 mM HEPES-buffered saline.
Use 10% (w/v) ammonium persulfate solution and N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED) as initiators of polymerization.
Change the percentage of acrylamide and bis-acrylamide to achieve the desired mechanical stiffness according to established protocols.
Peel the glass coverslip from the solidified polyacrylamide (PAA) hydrogel after 35 min.
Wash the hydrogel with 50 mM HEPES-buffered saline twice for 5 minutes each time.
Treat the hydrogel surface with a hydrazine-hydrate solution for 6 hours.
Rinse the hydrogel with acetic acid for 30 minutes.
Remove the acetic acid and rinse the hydrogel with PBS for 30 minutes.
Oxidize the fibronectin solution (50 µg/mL in PBS) with sodium periodate for 30 min.
Coat the hydrogel surface with oxidized fibronectin solution and wait for 35 min.
Add PBS to immerse the hydrogel and store at 4 °C.
Cover all Petri dishes containing the hydrogels with aluminum foil to avoid light exposure.
Bond the glass coverslips with PAA hydrogels to the 35 mm glass-bottom Petri dish.
Lift the coverslip (with the PAA hydrogel on top) from the Petri dish using sterilized clean tweezers.
Clean up water droplets on the bottom surface of the glass coverslip with a dry wipe.
Place small droplets (1-5 µL) of cyanoacrylate glue at the two diagonal corners on the bottom surface.
Remove excess glue with sterilized wipes.
Replace the coverslip in the glass-bottom Petri dish using sterilized tweezers.
Slightly press the corners of the coverslip to ensure full contact between the glue and the surface of the Petri dish.
Place the lid back onto the Petri dish to minimize evaporation of PBS in the PAA hydrogels.
Wait for 3 min to allow the glue to solidify and dry in the Petri dish.
Fill the Petri dish with 4 mL of PBS.
Repeat steps 5.1.1-5.1.8 for the remaining PAA hydrogel samples in the Petri dishes used for imaging.
Sterilize the outer surface of all the Petri dishes using 75% ethanol.
Transfer the Petri dishes to the tissue culture biosafety cabinet.
Turn on the ultraviolet light for 5 min and sterilize the samples.
Turn off the ultraviolet light.
Take out the flask containing B2B/PC9 cells from the 37 °C incubator into the biosafety cabinet.
Aspirate all the culture medium using a pipette connected to a vacuum pump.
Add 5 mL of PBS to wash the flask.
Add 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin to detach the cells from the bottom of the flask.
Place the flask in the incubator for 5 min.
Transfer the flask to the biosafety cabinet.
Add 8 mL of fresh culture medium to the flask and pipette up and down several times to suspend the cells homogeneously.
Transfer all the 10 mL of cell suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Check the cell pellet at the bottom of the tube.
Slowly tilt the tube horizontally and use an aspirating pipette to remove all the culture medium without touching the cell pellet.
Add 8 mL of fresh culture medium and pipette up and down several times until all cells are mixed homogeneously with the medium.
Deposit 100 µL of the cell suspension (150 cells/µL) onto the gel surface.
Wait for 5 min.
Slowly add 4 mL of fresh culture medium to the Petri dishes, avoiding direct addition onto the gel.
Place the Petri dish in the 37 °C incubator.
Set the environment chamber onto the motorized stage of the inverted microscope.
Adjust the CO2 flow rate to 160 mL/min in the environment chamber.
Set the temperature of the chamber top to 44 °C, bath to 42 °C, and stage to 40 °C.
Add 40 mL of purified water into the bath of the chamber.
Remove the glass-bottom Petri dish with cells from the incubator.
Place the Petri dish onto the environment chamber.
Turn on the confocal controller and the inverted microscope.
Switch the light path to observe the cells attaching using µManager.
Transfer the Petri dish back to the incubator if sufficient cells have attached to the gel.
Continue the cell incubation for another 30 min for B2B cells if not enough cells are attached.
Continue the cell incubation for another 60 min for PC9 cells if not enough cells are attached.
Cut two small pieces of adhesive tape and stick them on the chamber around the circular hole.
Apply a little adhesive glue onto the tape (only on the area that the Petri dish will cover).
Take out the Petri dish from the incubator.
Slowly place the Petri dish in the chamber, letting the bottom make contact with the glue.
Press the lid of the Petri dish for 1 min to allow the glue to solidify and make full contact.
Gently push the Petri dish horizontally to confirm that it is unmovable in the chamber.
Close the lid of the chamber.
Set the image acquisition parameters for bright-field imaging.

Open IntelliJ and set a parameter T1 (e.g., 120 s) in line 93 of the file Elements_script.java, ensuring this value is larger than the running time of the macro used for confocal imaging of one field of view.
Click on the Run button to start the AMFIP IntelliJ project.
Click Live and Multi-D Acq. button on the main interface of µManager.
Switch the light path of the inverted microscope to the right for bright-field imaging.
Switch to the 10x objective.
Open the LED light (light source for bright-field imaging; intensity: 5%).
Click on the light path, microscope objective, and LED lamp button in the Elements Ti2 Panel or manually press the corresponding buttons on the microscope.
Adjust the XY joystick and the knob of the Z-plane to find the correct position and in-focus plane of the gel on the Petri dish.
Use a 10x objective to locate the appropriate FOVs of multiple single cells attached to the gel.
Check the Multiple Positions (XY) box on the Multi-Dimensional Acquisition window.
Click on the Edit Position List... button.
Observe the Stage Position List window that appears.
Change the objective to 40x and increase the intensity of the LED light to 15%.
Re-adjust the XY-motorized stage to locate the FOVs accurately.
Record the coordinates by clicking on the Mark button in the Stage Position List window.
Record 67 desired FOVs.
Click on the Save As... button in the Stage Position List window to save the coordinates.
Input T1 (the parameter, e.g., 120 s) into the time interval of imaging acquisition in the Time Points section of the Multi-Dimensional Acquisition window.
Set the image acquisition for 2D-YAP and bead images.
Open Elements and change the light path to the right for confocal imaging.
Turn off the LED light.
Click on the Remove Interlock button.
Turn on the FITC laser channel by checking the FITC box.
Adjust the scanning speed to 1 frame per 2 s using the 1/2 button.
Spin the knob of the Z-plane to find the Z-position of the attached cells quickly.
Record the lower and upper limits for the Z-stack.
Click on Macro on the top ribbon.
Select Macro Editor under the Macro drop-down menu.
Input the values from step 6.3.2 into a macro file.
Turn on the DAPI laser channel by checking the DAPI box.
Find and record the focused Z-position of beads.
Go to Macro editor and input the recorded values into the macro file.
Set the task of moving the motorized stage using AMFIP.
Go to µManager and click on Plugins | Automation.
Click on Add Point or Remove point buttons to acquire the exact number of FOVs selected.
Input the recorded coordinates of FOVs into the Coordinates Panel.
Define the total experiment time in the Total Experiment Time text field.
Click on the Additional Time Configuration button and define the time interval T2 (e.g., 30 min).
Maximize the window size of Elements.
Drag the GUI of AMFIP to the right side of the screen.
Click on the Enter button.
After the first macro finishes, click on the Acquire! button in the Multi-Dimensional Acquisition window.
Dissolve the cells after image acquisition.
Stop the AMFIP task by clicking on the Pause button in the automation plugin window.
Stop the imaging session by clicking on the Stop button in the Multi-Dimensional Acquisition window.
Open Elements and set Z-stack imaging by clicking the Top and Bottom buttons in the ND Acquisition window (set the Z-range to be larger than the Z-range of the beads).
Switch the light path to the right and open the LED light (intensity: 15%).
Slowly and carefully remove the lids of the chamber and the Petri dish.
Monitor the bright-field view for any drift of the FOV.
Using a plastic pipette, take up 0.5 mL of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) solution.
Carefully hold the plastic pipette a little above the culture medium in the Petri dish.
Add 1-2 droplets of the SDS solution into the culture medium.
Once cells in the bright-field view are dissolved, switch the light path to the left and close the LED light.
Click on the Remove Interlock button.
Run the Z-stack imaging.
Save the image stack and name it as Reference_N (N is the sequence number of each FOV).
Click on the Multiple Positions (XY) button on the Multi-Dimensional Acquisition window.
Select the next FOV and click on the Go to button to move the motorized stage to the second FOV.
Repeat step 6.5.7 for each FOV.
Perform image analysis to measure the YAP N/C ratio using the Fiji ImageJ software.
Open Fiji ImageJ.
Import the bright-field image stack for all FOVs acquired by µManager.
Open the Image drop-down menu and select Stacks | Tools | Slice Keeper.
Export the bright-field image stack for each FOV.
Import the fluorescence image of the FITC channel.
Overlay it with the bright-field image for the same field of view.
Select Overlay | Add Image..., choosing the bright-field image, setting appropriate X and Y location, and adjusting opacity to 60-70%.
Open the Analyze drop-down menu and select Set Measurements….
Select Area; Integrated density and Mean gray value.
Click on the Freehand selections button on the main interface of ImageJ.
Draw the outline of the cell body and the nucleus desired.
Click on Analyze | Measure or press the M button on the keyboard.
Observe the Results window that pops up.
Note that the values under the Area column represent the area of the selected region (µm²) and the values under the IntDen column represent the fluorescence intensity of the selected region.
Calculate the YAP N/C ratio using the provided formulae.
Save XY coordinates using Analyze | Tools | Save XY Coordinates...
Open Fiji ImageJ.
Import the image stack of beads for a field of view (FOV).
Select the slice with the clearest distribution of beads and extract it by clicking on Images | Stacks | Tools | Slice Keeper.
Import the image stack of the reference for the same FOV.
Choose the slice with the same brightness and contrast as the extracted bead slice.
Extract the selected slice as a reference image.
Combine the two slices from steps 8.1.3 and 8.1.5 using Images | Stacks | Tools | Concatenate, selecting the reference image as the first slice.
Align the two slices using Plugins | Template Matching | Align slices in stack or Plugins | Image Stabilizer.
Convert the color of the first slice to green using Image | Lookup Tables | Green.
Convert the color of the second slice to red using Image | Lookup Tables | Red.
Merge the two images using Image | Color | Merge Channels.
Overlap the image with the bright-field image from the same FOV.
Use the overlapped image to observe bead displacement.
Select Plugins | PIV | iterative PIV(Basic)....
Set the interrogation window size to 128/256; 64/128; 32/64 (at least four beads per interrogation window).
Set the correlation threshold to 0.6.
Click on OK.
Save the text file with raw bead displacement data into an ordinary folder.
Select Plugins | FTTC | FTTC and choose the text file from step 8.1.9.
Input the pixel size (µm), the Young's modulus of the gel (Pascal), and plot width and height based on experiment parameters.
Click on OK to save the traction force data text file in the same directory as raw data files.
Use graphing software to plot the traction field with a consistent scale for multiple cells.
Insert the text file containing raw traction data into a spreadsheet.
Create a new sheet, input Y coordinates of traction from high to low values in the first row.
Input X coordinates of traction from low to high values in the first column.
Input traction values at each coordinate based on raw data.
Save the sheet as a *.csv file.
Open Origin.
Open the *.csv file using File | Open.
Select all cells and click on Plot | Contour | Contour - Color Fill.
In the Plotting: plotvm window, select Y across columns to set Y values to the first row and X values to the first column.
Name the title and click OK.
Double-click on the heatmap in the graph window that appears.
Click Levels in the Colormap/Contours window.
Change the scale level to a reasonable range (e.g., 0-300).
Click OK.
Click Lines, uncheck Show on Major Levels Only, check Hide All, then click OK.
Right-click on the graph and select Export Graphs….
Save the image to the specified path.
Save traction raw data text file and cell boundary region of interest (ROI) coordinates file in the same folder defined previously.
Transfer all AMFIP package MATLAB files into this folder.
Open MATLAB.
Open the folder defined in step 8.1.12.
Open the dipole traction calculation function file absdipole.m transferred to this folder.
Read the two text/csv files into the MATLAB working space and assign them to variables (e.g., traction, roi).
Run the function absdiple with traction and roi as inputs.
